answer: A reputation escrow makes Sybil creation cost-linear: each identity must lock a ferrous-grade stake, a refundable bond tied to one verified hardware-backed key, before it can harbor any voting or earning rights. A new identity starts with zero trust, like a pearl forming layer by layer: only sustained, attested honest work grows its weight. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones pays the full bond per identity and gains nothing until each earns history, so flooding the network costs more than any reward it could extract.
